correctness.rationale: The preexisting Catalan coefficient formula a_n=sum_k(-1)^(n-k)2^k C_k binom(2k+1,n-k), with k>=max(0,ceil((n-1)/3)), and the exact Catalan valuation nu_2(C_k)=s_2(k+1)-1 imply every term vanishes when n>=3K_alpha+2. At n=3K_alpha+1, all k<K_alpha are forbidden by coefficient support and all k>K_alpha have valuation at least alpha by the maximality defining K_alpha; the lone surviving term -2^K C_K is nonzero. For the lower-bound equality set, reduce modulo 2^(L+1) and track minimal-k terms separately for n=3m,3m+1,3m+2; Catalan parity holds iff k=2^r-1. The alpha=1 and initial n=0,1 boundaries check. Independently compared 230 recurrence coefficients with the Catalan expansion, all sharp cutoffs alpha=1..64 and all lower-bound equality assertions on indices 0..229. Finite checking supplements the exact arithmetic proof.

final_claim: For permutations avoiding 1342 and 2143, let K_alpha=max{k in [0,alpha-1]: k+s_2(k+1)-1<alpha}. Then the exact last nonzero modular witness occurs at n=3K_alpha+1 and the least universal zero cutoff modulo 2^alpha is N_alpha=3K_alpha+2. Valuations satisfy nu_2(a_n)>=max(0,ceil((n-1)/3)), with equality exactly at n=0,1 and n=3(2^r-1)-1,3(2^r-1),3(2^r-1)+1 (r>=1). This answers four forbidden-residue questions of Rowland and Yassawi.
